candidates.title: Weekly US rail freight climbs 4.7% as intermodal surges 8.3%
candidates.excerpt: U.S. rail traffic rose 4.7% for the week ending November 21 from a year ago, the Association of American Railroads said, as intermodal volume again drove gains. Containers and trailers improved 8.3% compared with the same week in 2025, while commodity carloads edged up 0.5%. Six of the 10 carload commodity groups posted gains. Metallic ores and metals used in steelmaking led at 17.9%. Forest products rose 11% despite real estate market issues; petroleum and petroleum products improved 11.2%, and motor vehicles and parts rose 8.3% as year-end sales promotions outweighed higher interest rates. Farm products excluding grain and food were up 6.2%, and chemicals increased 2.1%. Four groups declined as grain fell 17.4%, the steepest drop. Coal was off 4.4%, while unspecified carloads were off 2.1%, and nonmetallic minerals such as sand and stone dropped 0.9%. candidates.title: New product improves cybersecurity for rail computer systems
candidates.excerpt: NEW YORK — An ongoing concern when configuring and installing information technology is software-hardware compatibility. Although this is not usually a major challenge, compatibility remains a requirement. Two companies recently announced new compatibility that can make life a little easier for railroaders. Cylus, which provides rail cybersecurity with its CylusOne product, and Moxa, a provider of edge connectivity and industrial computing, have partnered to deliver cybersecurity software for Moxa’s onboard rail computers. Edge computing is a hardware and software architecture that allows data to be processed where it is collected. Rather than processing data in the cloud or over large networks, the onboard computer does the hard work, reducing cloud communication needs and saving processing power and bandwidth. Joe Chacon, the Belt Railway’s digital media coordinator who formerly led Operation Lifesaver Illinois’ board of directors, said the Federal Railroad Administration provided feedback in the development of the PSA. candidates.excerpt: Maersk will revise several demurrage and detention tariffs in the United States and Canada from 1 January 2027, based on the applicable Price Calculation Date. The changes cover dry containers, operating and non-operating reefers, US rail ramps and equipment moving through Newark. Most of the revised daily rates are higher than their current levels. The updated tariffs are as follows: The amounts are charged per day according to the existing tier structure. Maersk will also revise US export detention free time for certain agricultural cargoes transported in dry or non-operating reefer containers. Hay shipments will receive 10 working days of free time when the Price Calculation Date falls between April and September. This will increase to 14 working days for shipments with a Price Calculation Date between October and March. Other agricultural products will receive seven working days of export detention free time.

candidates.excerpt: UK port congestion, empty-container restrictions add upward pressure to freight rates Congestion across the UK container logistics network is tightening effective vessel and equipment capacity, adding upward pressure to freight prices as carriers contend with import backlogs, schedule disruption and restrictions on empty-container returns. Maersk said in a Nov. 24 customer advisory that sustained high import volumes, network congestion, adverse weather and recent rail disruption had placed pressure on UK and Ireland port and landside operations. Vessel delays and high use of inland storage were compounding the disruption, with the carrier warning that normal network fluidity would take time to restore despite services beginning to recover. Empty-equipment bottlenecks have become an additional constraint. candidates.title: Stalled exits drive growth in GP and LP financing
candidates.excerpt: Stalled exits drive growth in GP and LP financing Lending to general partners (GPs) and limited partners (LPs) is growing significantly, driven by a need for liquidity and an appetite to invest. Fokke Lucas, a partner at 17Capital, said GP and LP financing is currently one of the biggest growth areas in fund finance. “That’s where we are seeing increased volume,” he said. “We expect to continue to invest significantly in that space. We believe we are well positioned for the opportunity as we have one of the largest dedicated teams and pools of capital for this opportunity.” The main driver is the slowdown in exits, he said. Managers are holding on to portfolio companies for longer to grow their value, so less cash is being returned to LPs and GPs, which is pushing up borrowing against fund stakes. “We see that it continues to be driven by the prolonged [illiquidity]… It sounds a bit like Groundhog Day,” Lucas said. “It just continues to push out these exits.” Read more: Insurers drive

candidates.title: Union Pacific police in shootout after alleged train robbery on southern California freight line
candidates.excerpt: Two men were arrested after a shooting involving Union Pacific Railroad Police investigating suspected cargo theft near the busy Tehachapi Loop on Nov. 12. No injuries were reported, according to the Kern County Sheriff’s Office and reported in local media. The shooting occurred about 10:40 p.m. near Highway 58 and Broome Road, east of the loop. Railroad (NYSE: UNP) police were patrolling the area in response to recent thefts from trains when they discovered an open cargo-container door, authorities said. Officers began investigating, and a shooting occurred, according to the sheriff’s account. candidates.title: U.S. rail traffic up 7.8% as intermodal leads gainers
candidates.excerpt: U.S. rail traffic increased 7.8% in the week ended Oct. 24 compared with the same week in 2025, as growth in intermodal shipments outpaced gains in carloads, Association of American Railroads data shows. Weekly intermodal volume, which includes containers and trailers, rose 11.3%, while carload traffic increased 3.6%. Both measures grew faster than their respective year-to-date rates. Eight of the 10 carload commodity groups recorded year-over-year increases. Petroleum and petroleum products led percentage growth, rising 15.4%, followed by motor vehicles and parts at 15.3%. Forest products increased 11.7%, and metallic ores and metals gained 11.6%. Farm products excluding grain, and food fell 3.7%, while grain posted a rare decline at 1.4%. For the first 42 weeks of 2026, combined U.S. rail traffic increased 3.8% from the same period in 2025. Carloads rose 2.7%, while intermodal traffic was better by 4.7%. candidates.title: Backlog grows as 35,000 containers await rail service at LA–Long Beach
candidates.excerpt: Nearly 35,700 import containers were waiting for on-dock trains at the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach this week, as record cargo volumes and reported railcar shortages slowed the movement of freight inland. Of the 35,688 containers awaiting rail service on Oct. 26, 10, 562 had been on the terminals for at least nine days, according to The Dwell’s compilation of the ports’ daily rail reports. The figures count individual containers, rather than twenty-foot-equivalent units, or TEUs, the standard measure of port cargo volume. The backlog was more severe at Los Angeles, where 8,133 of the 19,626 containers awaiting trains had waited nine days or longer. At Long Beach, 2,429 of 16,062 rail-bound containers had reached that threshold. That put the share of longer-waiting containers at 41.4% in Los Angeles, compared with 15.1% in Long Beach.
